note: Who makes the external parts (scripts/part_makers.gd). The parts the yards always had are Northstar Commercial's: sold everywhere at list price. Each entry below adds a maker's version of a part (module id <part>__<maker>), with multipliers on the base part's numbers: mass, cost, thrust, heat (heat made), cooling (heat shed by radiators), power (drawn), fuel, lift, retro, rcs, drive (added to the drive's speed fraction), wear (how fast it wears). Prices: home_discount at the maker's home system, import_duty everywhere else. Makers come from data/world/manufacturers.json.

parts.pitch: More thrust for less mass, and it runs hot. Strict tolerances: it wears fast if you don't look after it.
Heavy, expensive and notoriously difficult to kill. Wears at less than half the usual rate.
A big engine for big freighters: half again the thrust, twice the mass, and a heat problem.
Ugly, cheap and a bit weak. Mechanics love it; nobody else notices it.
Sheds more heat and lasts. A little heavier, a little dearer, very well documented.
Weighs almost nothing. Repairing it takes the right materials, and it knows when you didn't use them.
The same fuel in a tank that weighs a lot less. For range, at a price.
Bolt-on and bigger: a fifth more fuel, a little more tank.
A cheap tank with industrial pumps. Heavier than it needs to be.
Exposed rails, obvious retrofit space, and cheaper.
Massive gear for heavy landings: more lift, and it outlasts the ship.
Crisp, strong and light. Fussy about maintenance.
They push. Mostly in the direction asked. Cheap.
More braking from a lighter fairing. Wants looking after.
A faster drive: a third again the speed between stars, more power, and strict tolerances.
Heavy and slow to wear out. The drive you want when the nearest yard is very far away.
